cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Apologize for the Lie
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You gave me the rescue dog's photo and hid the page about chewing furniture. That's not a complete handover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'd have said no. He needed a home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you knew the missing page mattered. Please acknowledge that before we discuss where he sleeps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for any damage. Can we just settle him in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. But 'I'll pay' is a budget, not an apology. Tell me you should have shown me the page.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 evaluates the selective rescue information as an incomplete handover. A3 seeks acknowledgment of the omission, and A5 corrects B4's payment offer as the wrong category of response.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 admits disclosure would have changed A's decision; A3 uses that admission. B4 offers compensation and immediate dog care, causing A5 to agree to settling the dog while retaining the apology request.

relationship.evidence: B2 prioritizes a dog needing a home; B4 offers to shoulder damage. A responds to these defensible aims instead of requiring B to confess the rescue itself was wrong.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4's practical next step yet refuses to let a financial repair substitute for disclosure acknowledgment.

specificity.evidence: A1 gives the photo and withheld chewing warning; A3/B4 sleeping and settling explain the immediate household task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's budget/apology distinction is a brief correction directed at B's money offer, not a summary of the cards.
